properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 19 at 6:01PM MDT until September 19 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Lee burn scar in...
Central Rio Blanco County in northwestern Colorado...

* Until 900 PM MDT.

* At 601 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Lee Burn Scar. Between 0.3 and 0.5 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 3 inches in 1
hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other
loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Lee Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Lee Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central Rio Blanco County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Lee Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Hardee County in central Florida...
Northwestern DeSoto County in south central Florida...
Northwestern Highlands County in south central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 3 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Sebring, Avon Park, Arcadia, Southeast Arcadia, Sweetwater, Zolfo
Springs, Gardner, Brownville, Crewsville, Limestone, Nocatee,
Avon Park Executive Airport and Sebring Shores.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

South Central Valencia County in central New Mexico...

Bernardo, or 20 miles southwest of Belen, moving east at 15 mph.

roofs, siding, and trees.

and Las Nutrias.

Markers 171 and 175. Interstate 25 between Mile Markers 175 and 193.

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 19 at 1:47PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of low pressure systems will move through the panhandle
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the light rain will continue Saturday evening before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday night into Sunday
morning bringing moderate to heavy rain fall. Rain showers will
then take over on Sunday that may bring occasional moderate to
heavy rainfall as well.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

with flash flooding over recent burn scars.

County Wyoming.

poor drainage and urban areas.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 19 at 11:59AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
ESFRIW

Periods of showers and thunderstorms are expected across the northern
half of Wyoming Saturday and Sunday as a wet weather system shifts
east across the state. This weather system is funneling abundant
tropical moisture into northern and eastern portions of the state
with it's eastward progression. Given the high moisture content, many
thunderstorms could feature heavy rainfall and possibly lead to
localized flooding. Poor drainage areas, urban areas, and steep
terrain will be the most susceptible locations for this isolated
flooding.

Many locations could see an additional 0.5" to 1.25" of rain through
Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling quickly in
thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

NWSheadline: Showers and Thunderstorms Could Produce Heavy Rainfall and Localized Flooding through Sunday

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows
remain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 412 AM AKDT, gage reports indicated widespread moderate to
heavy rain across the Chena River Basin over the past several
days. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain has fallen this week.

- High water levels will continue to work through the Fairbanks,
Badger, and North Pole region along the Chena and Little Chena
Rivers. Use extra caution on and along the rivers as water levels
continue to run at near record to record levels for this time of
year. The Chena River near Two Rivers is dropping but remains
bankfull. The Chena River below Hunts Creek is dropping but
remains bankfull. The Chena River below Moose Creek Dam is
cresting. The Chena River at Fairbanks will be cresting Saturday
afternoon. We are expecting rivers to remain high through the
weekend but gradually drop towards more normal levels through the
week.

At 4:00am the stage was 15.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.2 feet.

Saturday.

Flood Stage is 24.5 feet.

Saturday.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

High water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next
few days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water
levels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of
next week.

Locations:

* Communities across the lower Kuskokwim River and its tributaries,
including, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,
Napaskiak, Napkiak, Kasigluk, Nunapitchuk, and Atmauluak.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* High water in the Kuskokwim and other area rivers (e.g. Kwethluk
River, Johnson River, etc) may inundate low-lying areas in the
aforementioned communities, nearby fish camps, and other lowlands.

Details/Analysis [What's causing this?]:

* Rainfall: The Kuskokwim River basin, from the mouth at Kuskokwim
Bay upstream to the headwaters in the Alaska Range and Kilbuck
Mountains, has received approximately 150 to 200 percent of normal
rainfall this summer (June to August). These rains have continued
into September, with nearly the entire basin near or exceeding 200
percent of rainfall, with much of that rainfall occurring over the
last few days.

* Persistent High Water: This heavy rainfall has resulted in
anomalously high water levels being routed down from the Upper
Kuskokwim to the Lower Kuskokwim. The river gages at McGrath and
Crooked Creek are near or exceeding record levels for this time of
year. The water levels at these stations have crested in the last
week, suggesting that the water inflow to the lower Kuskokwim
Communities may be on the decrease soon.

* Compounding Factors: In addition to the recent rainfall and
elevated river levels, strong coastal winds brought several feet of
surge to the coast, causing elevated water levels near the mouth of
the Kuskokwim River. This effectively reduces the slope of the
river, slowing drainage and resulting in water becoming backed up.

* Forecast Thoughts: A shift in the weather pattern will bring
conditions favorable for water levels to decrease. Northerly winds
will increase Saturday and continue into early next week to 20 to
30 kt, with higher gusts possible at times, and bring cooler and
drier air to the region. Precipitation will be sparse and generally
light. Additionally, tidal models indicate a slight negative surge
along the coast due to the multi-day period of strong northerly
winds, potentially assisting drainage of water from the lower
Kuskokwim River.

Look Ahead:

* After a period of weather conditions favorable for receding water,
confidence is growing that another strong Bering Sea storm will
affect western Alaska late next week (Sept 23-26). A return to
southerly winds and higher coastal water in conjunction to heavy
rainfall may exacerbate river conditions once again, particularly
on the smaller tributaries such as the Kwethluk and Johnson Rivers.
However, details remain uncertain at this time as confidence is low
in storm track and intensity. Fortunately, natural tidal cycles in
Bethel and the rest of the lower Kuskokwim favor lower tides than
usual for this timeframe which may offset any additional water or
surge.

NWSheadline: HIGH WATER LEVELS ACROSS THE LOWER KUSKOKWIM

* WHERE...All of north Alabama and southern middle Tennessee.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Saturday.

illnesses.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.
